learning_outcomes.text: Know the different types of systems available for cold production.
Draw the processes of a single or multiple vapor compression cycle in property diagrams.
Apply mass and energy balances to components and/or single and multiple vapor compression cycles.
Understand the meaning of the different psychrometric properties.
Calculate humid air properties using the psychrometric chart.
Apply mass and energy balances to control volumes where psychrometric processes occur.
Know the key aspects of the combustion process and balance a chemical combustion reaction.
Apply mass and energy balances to control volumes in a combustion reaction.
Calculate and differentiate the calorific values of a fuel.

syllabus_topics: Non-reactive mixtures of ideal gases and psychrometry
assessment_rules: Students can choose between two assessment modalities. Modality 1 (continuous) includes a final exam (80%), oral defense of practicals (10%), and seminars (10%). For Modality 1, a minimum of 4.5 out of 10 in the final exam and 40% (4 out of 10) in both the oral defense and seminars is required; otherwise, the final grade is capped at 4. Modality 2 (final) consists solely of a single final exam, which is also applied to extraordinary calls.
